open.title: Taxi: discover taxi kiosks and handle taxi flights
open.head: 19786895e3bb399a95576295916318b4dfc9bbc2
open.author: djjuno
open.body:
## Summary

The taxi window was empty on game_rework and taking a flight did nothing: no taxi nodes were ever sent, and `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF) had no handler. This PR adds kiosk discovery and the flight handler. The player pays and is teleported to the destination.

This is the taxi part of #599 without the bind point parts it sat on. The rest of the taxi work is split into smaller follow up PRs, each built on this one:

| PR | Branch | What it adds | Needs |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| #608 | `fix/taxi-fares` | The fare the taxi map shows, no purchase in combat or without the credits | this PR |
| #609 | `fix/taxi-ride` | The holo cab ride along the route's splines, no casts or attacks on a rider, the landing line | #608 |

## Cause

The taxi map only offers routes through nodes the server says the character discovered, and the server never sent any. Taking a flight or shuttle sends `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF), which had no handler.

## Change

Kiosk nodes are discovered when the player comes within 30 units of a kiosk creature (`Creature2.taxiNodeId`) or talks to it, saved in a new `character_taxi_node` table (with migration), sent with `ServerTaxiNodeUnlock` (0x0186) when found and in `ServerFlightPathUpdate` (0x0188) at login. The flight handler reads the route as TaxiRoute ids, checks that the legs chain from a kiosk near the player and are neutral or of the player's faction, charges the sum of `TaxiRoute.price` and teleports the player to the last leg's node. #608 replaces that price with the one the map shows.

## Migration

This adds the `CharacterTaxiNode` migration and changes `CharacterContextModelSnapshot.cs`. #601 also adds one (`CharacterBind`). Each PR builds and applies on its own against game_rework, but if both merge, the second one needs its migration and snapshot rebased on the first. I can do that once the first one is in.

In #599 this migration came after the bind one. Here its Designer file is the game_rework model plus the taxi node table only. Most of the diff is that generated Designer file (3,039 lines); the rest is about 420 lines.

## Testing

Server only, as in #599. The branch is based on the current game_rework (1f643f63) and the full solution builds in Release with 0 errors and no new warnings. It has not been run in a client on game_rework.

AI (Claude) helped write these changes.

open.title: Galactic Archive: unlock articles from achievements and quests
open.head: e41fb57514cc202425430684e11e5fdd8f1b71f0
open.author: rebaserHEAD
open.body:
Gets the Galactic Archive working. Articles and their entries unlock from `ArchiveEntryUnlockRule` when an achievement is completed or a quest is handed in, the state is saved per character, and the client gets every article back after a world change.

Builds on #587 (article id width), so that commit shows here until it's merged.

- `GlobalGalacticArchiveManager` builds the rule index at start-up: for each achievement or quest, which entry slots in which articles it opens. An entry can sit in more than one article, so one rule can open slots in several. 847 of the 867 rules are used; the other 20 point at entries that aren't in any article and get skipped (counted in the start-up log line).
- `GalacticArchiveManager` on the player holds the articles, saved to a new `character_archive_article` table (migration included). The two flag words are stored as the client uses them.
- Hooked in at the end of `QuestManager.QuestComplete` and `CharacterAchievementManager.CompleteAchievement`. A quest counts once it's handed in, not when it's achieved.
- Handlers for `ClientGalacticArchiveUnlock` and `ClientGalacticArchiveViewed`. The client applies both locally before sending them, so the server records them and sends nothing back.
- Every stored article is sent again after each world entry, since the client drops the whole archive on a world change.
- An article's title reward (`characterTitleIdReward`) is granted once every entry in it is unlocked.
- `[GameData]` on `ArchiveArticle`, `ArchiveEntry` and `ArchiveEntryUnlockRule`.

Not covered: path mission rules are loaded but nothing completes a path mission on `game_rework` yet, so they never fire. There's no backfill either, so a character only picks up articles from completions after this lands.

Tested on a local server. Granted every achievement that unlocks something (180) and compared each saved article against what the rule table predicts: 134 articles, all match. Quest unlocks checked with two hand-ins, and an article opened in the panel stays read across world changes. The title reward is the one piece I couldn't reach in testing: only two articles carry one, and nothing I could trigger completes either of them.

open.title: Fix exception when activating a datacube the character already has
open.head: f88b196f11b909b4e0db94db2affff3c585d971f
open.author: djjuno
open.body:
## What was broken

Using a datacube (a lore object whose creature has `DatacubeId` set) works the first time. Using it again, or using another copy of the same datacube, throws `ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added` in the world server. The packet handler catches and logs the error, but the player gets nothing back, so the datacube does not play again the way it does after a normal first use.

## Cause

`SimpleEntity.OnActivate` always calls `DatacubeManager.AddDatacube` when the creature has a datacube. `AddDatacube` creates a new entry and adds it with `Dictionary.Add`, which throws when the character already has that datacube. `OnActivateCast` in the same class already checks `GetDatacube` first and only adds when it is missing; `OnActivate` did not.

## Fix

`OnActivate` now looks the datacube up first. If the character does not have it, it is added as before (full progress). If the character already has it, the existing entry is sent to the client again with `SendDatacube`, which matches what `OnActivateCast` does for known datacubes and lets the client show or play it again. Nothing changes for a datacube used for the first time.

## How it was tested

* Full solution build (`dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx -t:Rebuild`): 0 errors, and the same 7 warnings as `game_rework` before the change (no new warnings).
* There is no test project in the solution. I checked the code path by reading it: `ClientActivateUnitHandler` calls `OnActivate`, which calls `AddDatacube`, which calls `Dictionary.Add` with no existence check. `OnActivateCast` in the same class already guards against this.

AI tools (Claude) helped find this bug and write the fix; I reviewed and tested the change.

open.title: Fix server dirty character jobs never ending when a character is marked dirty again during a run
open.head: 8ca89ccb31c20a286a64ac632fca8885d812cba5
open.author: djjuno
open.body:
## What was broken

`CharacterDirtyRealmScheduledJob` and `CharacterDirtyStatsScheduledJob` in the group server can get stuck in a busy loop that never finishes. While stuck, the job keeps picking the same character, publishes the same stale update over and over, never clears the flag, and never reaches any other dirty character. Because both jobs are `[DisallowConcurrentExecution]`, the run never ends and later runs never start, so realm and stats updates for the other group members stop going out.

## Cause

Each job uses one injected `GroupContext` for the whole run and loops on `CharacterRepository.GetNextCharacterWithDirtyRealm()` (or `...DirtyStats()`). The query is a tracking query, so once a character has been loaded in that context, later queries return the instance that is already tracked and do not refresh its values.

The sequence that triggers it:

1. The job loads character A, sets `RealmDirty = false` and saves.
2. A message handler in another scope (for example `PlayerWorldUpdatedHandler` or `PlayerWorldZoneUpdatedHandler`) sets `RealmDirty = true` for A again in the database.
3. The next query in the job matches A in the database, but returns the tracked instance, which still says `RealmDirty = false`.
4. The job sets it to false again. EF sees no change, `SaveChangesAsync` writes nothing, and the database still says dirty.
5. The next query returns A again, forever.

The stats job is the most exposed, since stats change often and it runs every 2 seconds. The group and member lookups inside the loop also load other characters into the same context, so any of them can end up stale the same way.

## Fix

Each character is now processed in its own DI scope created from `IServiceScopeFactory`. The repository, `GroupContext`, `IInternalMessagePublisher` and the `Character` are resolved from that scope, so every iteration starts with a fresh context and reads the current database values. The publisher and the context come from the same scope, so outbox messages are still saved together with the flag change. The rest of the job logic is unchanged.

## How it was tested

* Full solution build (`dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx -t:Rebuild`): 0 errors, and the same 7 warnings as `game_rework` before the change (no new warnings).
* There is no test project in the solution, so I wrote a small throwaway console harness (not part of this PR) that references the group server, uses the EF Core InMemory provider, seeds two dirty characters, and marks the first one dirty again from a separate context right after the job's first save. The job was given a 3 second cancellation token.
  * Before the fix: both jobs ran until cancelled, about 20,000 (realm) and 30,000 (stats) `SaveChanges` calls in 3 seconds, and both characters were still dirty at the end. The second character was never processed.
  * After the fix: both jobs returned on their own in about 350 ms with 3 saves, and no character was left dirty.
* We also saw this on a live server: the realm job resent the same stale realm update to the client about 35 times a second, most characters stayed realm dirty, and other group server work queued behind it.

AI tools (Claude) helped find this bug and write the fix and the test harness; I reviewed and tested the change.

open.title: implement SpellEffect 73 ModifySpellCooldown
open.head: e100f4c29a1571a7181d06967ed8133612d99074
open.author: derdotte
open.body:
# Implement spell effect type 73 (ModifySpellCooldown)

Base: `expedition-evil-from-the-ether`. Independent of the heal work.

## Why

Type 73 is the most common spell effect type the server does not handle: 522 `Spell4Effects` rows on 467 spells, 382 of them class abilities. Without a handler those effects are silently ignored, so cooldown resets and reductions (Recharge, Onslaught, AMP cooldown reductions, ...) do nothing.

## What the effect does

Each row has four fields:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `dataBits00` scope | which cooldowns it matches: 0 = base spell id, 1 = `Spell4` id, 2 = spell group id, 3 = `SpellCoolDown` id |
| `dataBits01` key | the id to match in that key space |
| `dataBits02` mode | 0 = multiply, can only shorten; 1 = multiply, unclamped; 2 = add milliseconds (negative = reduce), floored at 0; 3 = set to an absolute number of milliseconds |
| `dataBits03` magnitude | float; milliseconds for modes 2 and 3, a factor for modes 0 and 1 |

Two things happen when the effect lands:

1. Every matching cooldown that is **running** is re-armed from its remaining time. A spell that is not on cooldown is not given one.
2. If the effect has a lifetime (`CancelOnly`, or delay + duration > 0: 85 of the 522 rows), the modifier is **held** and applied to every cooldown that starts while it is held, in the order the records were added. Removing it does not restore a cooldown it already shortened. The other 437 rows are one-shot.

## Implementation

- New handler, data class and the two enums (scope, mode) for `SpellEffectType.ModifySpellCooldown` (the enum member already existed).
- The arithmetic is shared with the existing `SetSpellCooldownByBaseSpell`, whose `type` parameter turned out to be this mode field.
- A per-player list of held records, folded into new cooldowns server-side so the server's own timer is authoritative.

### What is sent to the client

The client applies its own copy of the modifier to the duration of any cooldown node it has to create, so a reduction already folded in by the server would be applied twice. A new cooldown is therefore **sent with the duration before the server's own fold** and **stored with the folded value**. The one-shot re-arm sends nothing, because the client performs the same re-arm itself when the effect arrives.

## Bug fixes this needed

These are in cooldown code this feature is the first caller of:

1. The cooldown setters threw on a negative value. All 145 mode-2 magnitudes are negative, so the value is now floored at 0.
2. `SetSpellCooldown` threw when the `Spell4` row or base info was missing. 7 shipped rows name a missing `Spell4Base` id and 16 rows have key 0; both now mean "nothing matches".
3. `SetSpellCooldownByGroupId` threw if any unrelated spell in the dictionary had a missing row. It skips such entries now.
4. `SetSpellCooldownByGroupId` and `SetSpellCooldownByBaseSpell` could not emit `ServerCooldown`. Both take an `emit` argument now.
5. `ISpellInfo.Cooldowns` can contain `null`; guarded.

## Second commit: send the cooldown node types the client has

`ServerCooldown` carries a type, and the client keeps one cooldown node per (type, key). The server only ever sent type 1 (per spell). That left two gaps:

| type | what it is | key | what the server did |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | global cooldown | `Spell4.spellCoolDownIdGlobal` | tracked server-side, never sent |
| 1 | per-spell cooldown | `Spell4` id | sent |
| 2 | cooldown shared by every spell with the same `SpellCoolDown` id | `SpellCoolDown` id | tracked server-side, never sent |

So sibling spells that share a cooldown showed no cooldown on the action bar, and `Property.CooldownReductionModifier` (136) was declared but never read. The client does not apply that property to a duration the server sends, so if the server doesn't, nothing does.

This commit:

1. Emits a type 2 node for every `SpellCoolDown` id a spell carries, mirroring the client's own sender.
2. Gives a shared cooldown the duration the client gives it, `SpellCoolDown.cooldownTime`, falling back to the spell's own cooldown when the row has none.
3. Applies `CooldownReductionModifier` to the cooldown the server starts, for spells tagged Assault, Support or Utility, with the client's truncation to whole milliseconds. The property defaults to 1.0, so nothing changes unless something modifies it. A value of zero or less is treated as "no modifier".
4. Emits a type 0 node for the global cooldown (including the reset when a cast is cancelled by movement). The server's own dictionary stays keyed by `globalCooldownEnum`; only the wire value changes.

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** `cooldownIds` is read by `Spell.CheckCast`, so a shared cooldown whose `SpellCoolDown` row is longer or shorter than the spell's own cooldown now gates casting differently. This matches the client, but it affects every spell with a shared cooldown id (about 2,900 `Spell4` rows).

The client never shortens a running type-0 node, so a global cooldown sent shorter than the one already running is ignored by the client.

`CooldownReductionModifier` has no base value of its own in this server: it falls through `CalculateDefaultProperty` to the `CreatureLevel` table, where it happens to land on a column holding 1.0. Worth a separate issue.

tested **In game** (cast through the command system, because tiering up spells in the limited action set is not implemented; the cooldown node changes were applied during the test): The cooldowns that were running were modified and the times shown in the client matched the expected values exactly.

## Known limits

- The client's `max(delay, duration)` special case (one spell flag) is not modelled; it changes no row's held/one-shot classification.
- Casting the same spell again appends a second record, as the client does.
- A scope-2 record is a broadcast (group 475 covers 201 spells); only running cooldowns are touched.
- Six scope-2 mode-3 rows cannot start a cooldown, only shorten a running one, as in the client.

open.title: Entitlements: give every character the base entitlements of a full account
open.head: 163666c34b0a8efcd92fa062efd265751f4e77f1
open.author: rebaserHEAD
open.body:
Every account on a stock server looks like a trial account to the client. Its trade script (`trading.lua`) and both marketplace scripts refuse to open unless the player holds `EconomyParticipation`, and without `BaseCharacterProgressionCaps` and `BaseCurrencyCaps` the client caps level at 20 and currency at 500,000 and 5,000. Nothing on the server grants those, and the GM command can't either.

The blocker is how the server reads the `Entitlement` table's flags. Bit `0x2` was treated as disabled, so `CanUpdateEntitlement` refused every entitlement carrying it and `GetPremiumModiferValue` zeroed any reward property that reads one. The client reads that bit as hidden: it leaves the entitlement out of its UI but still stores and counts it. Every one of the base entitlements carries it.

- `EntitlementFlags.Disabled` is now `Hidden`, and neither check refuses it any more.
- Every character gets `BaseCharacterProgressionCaps`, `BaseCurrencyCaps`, `EconomyParticipation`, `GuildsAccess`, `FullSocialParticipation`, `CREDDUsage` and `InGameCSAccess` when it loads, if it doesn't already hold them.
- New character entitlements are marked for insert. They were saved as an update to a row that didn't exist, which fails the first time anything grants one.
- A small one while I was in there: the entitlement value check built its error message from `Entry` before it was set.

Tested on a local server with both test accounts' entitlements cleared first. Both characters were given the seven entitlements on login and they saved cleanly, and the trade window now gets past the client's check and sends `ClientP2PTradingInitiateTrade` (there's no trade handling yet, so that's as far as it goes). I haven't levelled a character past 20 to watch the level cap lift.

open.title: Fall back to the player's last open world position when leaving a content instance
open.head: 7fa2c35920668925481a3aea01b680d0f632136d
open.author: Hawkeyee101
open.body:
`ContentMapInstance.GetPlayerReturnLocation` only has a return location for players that entered through matching, and otherwise returns null (`// TODO: fallback to default return location`). Players that enter an instance another way (a GM teleport, a portal, a script) have nowhere to go when they leave it, for example through an instance exit portal.

Players now keep a `ReturnPosition`: the position they were at when they last left a map that isn't a content instance for a different world. `GetPlayerReturnLocation` uses it as the fallback. It's only applied once the teleport succeeds (in `OnAddToMap`), so a failed teleport leaves it untouched, and it's saved on the character (`returnWorldId`, `returnLocationX/Y/Z`, migration `CharacterReturnPosition`), so it survives a server restart.

Tested on a local server: after entering an adventure from Thayd with a teleport, `ReturnPosition` holds the spot in Thayd, and an exit portal script that teleports the player to it returns them there. The `GetPlayerReturnLocation` fallback itself (used when players are removed from an instance) wasn't tested separately.

open.title: NPE quest scripting example: Navigating Nexus → Claim to Stake
open.head: 7975e0d47ef4b43b493884d0166c04f7370dac2a
open.author: cristian-custodio
open.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a **playable New Player Experience (world 3460) quest path** from **Navigating Nexus** through **Face of the Enemy** into **A Claim to Stake** (housing hologram).

**Primary goal: example / reference code to inspire more quest progress.**
NexusForever still has huge gaps in quest scripting. This branch is meant as a working pattern others can copy, not a finished NPE or a claim that all quests should look exactly like this. If it helps someone wire their first `TalkTo`, `EnterArea`, CSI, or map hand-off, it did its job.

Use it as inspiration for:

- Other NPE steps (Lots in Store, Bon Voyage, etc.)
- Zone quests elsewhere in the world
- Shared objective wiring (`SucceedCSI`, `EnterArea`, checklist bits, parent `EnterZone`)

## Why this matters

A lot of retail quest data already exists in tables/SQL; what’s missing is **server-side hooks and scripts**. This PR shows one end-to-end slice:

1. Discover quests / objectives (`!quest world`)
2. Wire objective types in core gameplay
3. Add map / quest / entity scripts for the story beats
4. Hand off between quests without fake auto-teleports where retail uses a projector

## Playable flow (Exile; Dominion mirrored)

| Step | Quest | What happens |
|------|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Navigating Nexus (10527 / 10532) | Jump / hoverboard / boosters → combat projector → force-complete + teleport into combat hologram |
| 2 | Face of the Enemy (10518 / 10524) | Combat cinematic → beasts → mines → turrets → legionnaires → force-complete + **grant housing** (player stays put) |
| 3 | A Claim to Stake (10525 / 10526) | Activate **housing hologram projector 73741** → housing plot → Protostar talks (sky/music “upload”) → find Phineas |

**Not in this PR:** Lots in Store! (10540), Bon Voyage, and later NPE.

## Detailed changes

### Core quest objective wiring

- `SucceedCSI` — CSI / activate paths update objectives
- `EnterArea` — from `WorldLocation2` indicators (minimum radius 5; many NPE markers use radius 1)
- `ActivateTargetGroupChecklist` — per-player bitfield slots via `QuestChecklistIdx`
- `EnterZone` — credit **leaf zone and all parents** (e.g. housing plot `5969` → hologram `4965`)
- `!quest world` — diagnostic listing quests tied to a world (default 3460)
- `!quest achieve` — GM-friendly: add if missing, clear sequential objectives, finish Achieved → Completed, chat feedback

### Activate / mount reliability

- Cast creature `Spell4IdActivate*` on activate-cast (hoverboard projector, etc.)
- Skip non-`IUnitEntity` activate targets (SimpleCollidable props crashed spell start)
- Don’t advance quests if activate cast fails; more reliable vehicle boarding

### NPE scripts (`NexusForever.Script.Main/Tutorial`)

- **TutorialMapScript** — auto-grant starter / combat / housing when prerequisites are met
- **NavigatingNexusQuestScript** — barrier despawn, combat hand-off teleport
- **FaceOfTheEnemyQuestScript** — cinematic on accept; on achieve force-complete + grant Claim to Stake (**no** auto-teleport to housing)
- **ClaimToStakeQuestScript** — EnterZone credit only if already inside housing hologram
- Combat AI: battle beasts, holo soldiers, interruptible hostile sim-turrets
- Objective rings, extra boosters, related helpers

### Client / interaction

- **Housing projector `73741`** — activate teleports into housing plot (spell itself is Activate + fullscreen only)
- **`ClientDialogOpened` → `ServerDialogEnd`** — fixes empty TalkTo “Uploading…” hang
- Sky / Music specialists cast NPE skybox / music change spells on TalkTo
- Null-safe `TakeDamage` (stops NRE spam)

## How to treat this as a template

If you’re adding another quest, the useful pieces to copy are:

1. **Wire the objective type once in core** if nothing calls `ObjectiveUpdate` for it yet.
2. Prefer **`[ScriptFilterOwnerId]` / `[ScriptFilterCreatureId]`** scripts over one-off hacks when behavior is content-specific.
3. **Map scripts** for grant / zone enter; **quest scripts** for accept / achieve / hand-off; **entity scripts** for interact / range / AI.
4. Match retail flow when possible (e.g. projector click vs silent teleport).
5. Add a small GM diagnostic when discovery is hard.

Imperfect or NPE-specific shortcuts are fine to leave behind—**the pattern is the point**.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh NPE char: Navigating Nexus completes into combat hologram
- [ ] Face of the Enemy: full combat path (or `!quest achieve 10518`) → grants 10525, **no** housing teleport
- [ ] Activate projector at ~`-176, -848, 626` → housing plot
- [ ] Talk Landscape ×2, Decor ×2, Sky, Music (no Uploading hang) → find Phineas
- [ ] Relog mid-quest does not soft-lock hand-offs
- [ ] Dominion path mirrors (10532 / 10524 / 10526)

## Notes for reviewers

- Target branch: **`game_rework`**.
- Intended as **inspirational / incremental** content for the community, happy to split, rename, or trim NPE-specific bits if that’s easier to land.
- World DB NPE SQL is assumed loaded for entity spawns; scripts bind by creature/quest id.

open.title: Coalesce movement relocations in the map grid action queue
open.head: 9289cbb1fdfb0ff06b90f124d2a9760a1d5655ab
open.author: Hawkeyee101
open.body:
Since c8a6d887 removed the relocation timer from the position command group (its message notes this might need to be revisited), every moving entity queues a relocation on every tick. `BaseMap` only processes `GridActionThreshold` (100) grid actions per update, so once a map has more moving entities than that the queue grows faster than it is processed. Every other grid action waits behind the backlog: adding or removing a player could take minutes, and the client gave up on the loading screen.

Movement relocations are now coalesced per entity. `GridEntity.RelocateOnMap` without a caller callback queues its relocation with a coalesce flag: while one is queued for the entity, a new relocation only updates the pending target, and the queued action moves the entity to the latest position when it is processed. Relocations with a caller callback (teleports) are queued as before.

Update: the first version coalesced relocations without a callback, but `RelocateOnMap` always passes the entity's own `OnRelocate`, so it never applied to movement. It now uses an explicit flag.

Tested on a local server with around 170 units walking splines on one map: players are added and removed right away, where before a player's add waited several minutes.

open.title: Generalise prerequisite evaluation and spell contexts
open.head: f366375743619958c8d93efcb9d7cee7fb63ac15
open.author: bobbygriz
open.body:
## Summary

This updates the prerequisite system to evaluate any `IUnitEntity` and provides explicit target context for relationship-based prerequisite checks.

It also completes the existing spell-level cast, persistence, effect-application, and proc prerequisite paths, while retaining the expedition branch's existing RapidTransport prerequisite validation behavior. No new prerequisite handlers or testing infrastructure are introduced.

## Changes

### Prerequisite evaluation

- Changed `IPrerequisiteCheck` and `IPrerequisiteManager` subjects from `IPlayer` to `IUnitEntity`.
- Added a manager overload accepting a target-context unit.
- Continued using the existing prerequisite-parameter factory for context creation.
- Added `Target`, `TaxiNode`, and nullable `CastResult` prerequisite parameters.
- Preserved the same parameter context through nested prerequisite evaluation.
- Updated existing handlers:
  - Unit-compatible handlers operate directly on `IUnitEntity`.
  - Player-specific handlers explicitly require an `IPlayer`.
  - Existing unimplemented handlers remain pass-through so they do not block spell casts.
- Corrected the native raw comparison mapping:
  - `3` is greater than.
  - `4` is greater than or equal.
  - `5` is less than.
  - `6` is less than or equal.
- Changed unsupported comparison branches in implemented handlers to fail closed.

### Spell prerequisite lifecycle

- Removed the player-only prerequisite bypass.
- Added caster-cast evaluation using `(caster, explicit target)`.
- Added target-cast evaluation using `(explicit target, caster)`.
- Added caster-persistence evaluation using `(caster, explicit target)`.
- Added target-persistence evaluation using `(explicit target, caster)`.
- Reused one explicit-target resolution path for validation, persistence, and execution.
- Missing required targets now fail the appropriate target-stage check or finish the active spell.
- Propagated `TaxiNode` into cast and persistence prerequisite parameters.
- Allowed caster- and target-cast prerequisite handlers to return a specific `CastResult`, with the existing stage-specific result retained as the fallback.

### Effect application

- Completed per-target effect prerequisite evaluation.
- Caster-apply prerequisites use `(caster, affected target)`.
- Target-apply prerequisites use `(affected target, caster)`.
- Removed the earlier context-free caster-apply check.
- Effect prerequisite failure skips application to that target rather than rejecting the entire cast.

### Proc integration

- Proc target prerequisites use `(trigger target, proc owner)`.
- Proc caster prerequisites use `(proc owner, trigger target)`.
- The accepted trigger target GUID is retained across the proc delay.
- Triggered spells receive the original target through `PrimaryTargetId`, preserving the correct context for downstream spell prerequisites.

### Spell metadata naming

Renamed the cached prerequisite properties to match the singular GameTable fields:

- `TargetCastPrerequisite`
- `CasterPersistencePrerequisite`
- `TargetPersistencePrerequisite`

### RapidTransport prerequisite

- Restored the existing `PrerequisiteType.RapidTransport` eligibility and affordability validation.
- Requires a player subject and valid taxi-node context.
- Validates taxi-node availability, auto-unlock level, destination data, minimum distance, and the RapidTransport cooldown formula.
- Uses the existing `IRapidTransportCostCalculator` and currency managers to check service-token or credit affordability.
- Returns `ServiceTokensInsufficentFunds` or `CasterVitalCostMoney` for the corresponding insufficient-funds cases, with `RapidTransportInvalid` as the general failure result.

This restores the expedition branch's server behavior; it does not claim that prerequisite type 269's client semantics have been confirmed by reverse engineering.

## Compatibility notes

- `Target` is the contextual counterpart to the evaluated `subject`; for target-side checks it therefore contains the caster.
- Runner overrides remain limited to the existing caster-cast stage.
- Cast-time target prerequisites apply only to the explicit target.
- Implicit AoE candidates are not evaluated with `TargetCastPrerequisite`.
- Unknown prerequisite types without a registered handler retain the manager's existing behavior.
- This does not implement new prerequisite handlers.

## Out of scope

- AoE target and preferred-target prerequisites.
- Effect persistence and target-suspend prerequisites.
- New test projects or prerequisite test infrastructure.
- Further interpretation of prerequisite type 269 beyond restoring the existing server behavior.

## Validation

- `dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx --no-restore --nologo --verbosity:minimal`
- Build completed with 0 errors.
- The existing 127 warnings remain.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- No tests were added or modified.

open.title: Fix players standing on platform entities
open.head: ce327232b3ce4f3c8ff360ffa135e6dafb4ff458
open.author: Hawkeyee101
open.body:
Three problems found with players standing on a spawned platform entity (a moving ship the players ride on). They are separate changes, happy to split them into their own PRs if preferred.

**Dismount throws on a non-vehicle platform.** `Player.Dismount` does `GetVisible<IVehicleEntity>(PlatformGuid)`. The platform can also be a normal entity the player stands on, so every user-initiated spell cast while standing on one threw `InvalidCastException`. It now only removes the passenger when the platform is a vehicle.

**Teleports keep the platform.** `OnTeleportToLocal` broadcasts the new position while the player is still attached to the platform. The client takes it as an offset from the platform and puts the player far outside the map (an empty void). A world change (`TeleportTo`) also kept the old map's platform guid. Both now call `SetPlatform(null)` first.

**Platform rotation ignored.** `PositionCommandGroup.Relocate` adds the platform position to the player's platform-relative position, but that position is in the platform's own turned frame. On a platform turned by -90° a player standing next to an NPC on it was placed 26.5 m away on the grid and could not interact with it. The relative position is now rotated by the platform's yaw (`Rotation.X`) before the platform position is added:

```
world = (x cos r + z sin r, y, -x sin r + z cos r) + platform position
```

Tested on a local server with a platform entity turned -90°: interaction range with NPCs on the platform is correct (checked against measured positions), casting spells on the platform no longer throws, and teleporting off the platform lands at the target position. Also tested with the platform flying (position keys) and turning 90° (rotation keys) with players and NPCs attached as passengers (`SetPlatform`): they stay in place on it and their server-side positions follow the platform through the turn.

open.title: GameTable: allow retry after cache initialization fails
open.head: ac913c09cd8bce2fdbcf1839fd33ea9c5662b794
open.author: SigmaCodez
open.body:
If cache preparation throws after CheckAndCleanupCache claims the initialization flag, cacheCheck remains 1. Every subsequent LoadWithCache call then stays in the polling loop, even after the filesystem problem has been repaired.

Reset the flag to 0 when cache preparation fails and rethrow the original exception. This allows a later or waiting caller to retry while preserving the existing successful initialization and cache invalidation behavior.

Add four GameTable test cases: recovery after a file blocks creation of the cache directory, recovery after a directory blocks writing cacheInfo.txt, deletion of stale cache files, and preservation of files with a matching module version. Recovery cases also verify that the creator was not invoked on failed preparation and that a subsequent load uses the newly written cache entry. Tests isolate process-wide state and release the old implementation's blocked worker after the timeout assertion, so failed regression tests do not hang the suite.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal
```

Before the fix: 2 recovery cases time out, 2 normal cases pass. After the fix: all 4 cases pass. `git diff --check` passes. Full-solution, Windows, in-game testing, and a concurrent stress test were not performed.

The current GameTableFactory cache call is commented out. This fixes the FileCache API; it does not claim an observed failure in the current default server startup or gameplay path. It does not enable the cache or change concurrent writes to individual cache entries.


Independent of #571–#575. Shares the GameTable test project and central package versions with #575. When combining them, keep both FileCacheTests.cs and WideStringTests.cs, with one project entry and one set of central package entries.

open.title: GameTable: read supplementary Unicode characters in wide strings
open.head: ac10142e60b6587b27b73da07ef9d4448f09a3af
open.author: SigmaCodez
open.body:
ReadWideString currently calls BinaryReader.ReadChar with UTF-16 encoding. Valid supplementary Unicode characters require a surrogate pair, but ReadChar supplies space for only one char. Reading such a character throws ArgumentException (output char buffer too small), including through StringTable.GetEntry.

Read UTF-16LE code units up to the null terminator and decode the complete byte sequence together. This preserves surrogate pairs, remains independent of the caller's BinaryReader encoding, and leaves bytes after the terminator available to the caller. Missing or truncated terminators still throw EndOfStreamException.

Add a GameTable test project with nine cases covering empty strings, ASCII, BMP Unicode, supplementary characters alone and mixed with other characters, StringTable offset lookups, following-byte preservation, and missing or truncated terminators.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal
```

Before the fix: 3 failures, 6 passes. After the fix: all 9 cases pass. `git diff --check` passes. Full-solution, Windows, and in-game validation were not performed. The regression is demonstrated with synthetic valid UTF-16 input; no claim is made that existing client data contains these characters.


Independent of #571–#574. Uses the same central test package versions; when combining these PRs, retain all test projects in the solution's Tests folder.

open.title: Network: reject reads past the end of a game packet
open.head: 00f8876ffa6ac239a7b98db153d9fd1c6a81734e
open.author: SigmaCodez
open.body:
`GamePacketReader.ReadBit()` casts `Stream.ReadByte()` directly to byte. At end of stream, the returned -1 becomes 0xFF, so truncated fields silently acquire set bits instead of reporting missing input. For example, reading a UInt32 from an empty stream currently produces UInt32.MaxValue.

Check the stream result before converting it and throw `EndOfStreamException` when no byte is available. Update the cached byte and bit position only after a successful refill, so repeated reads after EOF cannot expose stale bits. Valid bit order, cross-byte fields, padding resets, seeking, and zero-length reads are preserved.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Network.Tests/NexusForever.Network.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

Before the fix: 8 failures and 2 passes. After the fix: all 10 tests pass. The tests cover empty/exhausted streams, repeated EOF reads, truncated integers and strings, valid cross-byte fields, reset/seek behavior, and zero-length reads. `git diff --check` also passes.

The existing GameSession exception handler catches read failures before dispatching the message handler; this change does not add a disconnect policy. Full-solution builds, Windows, and in-game validation have not been performed. In-game validation should check whether any existing message definitions read beyond their actual payload, since such reads now fail explicitly.

This is independent of the functional changes in #571 and #572 and uses the same test-project registration and package versions.

open.title: Network: make listener startup and shutdown reliable
open.head: 39012c403e3d2fcdf0d9f7947c14c95ba5fd9c16
open.author: SigmaCodez
open.body:
Starting a listener on an occupied port currently faults the background task before it signals the startup event, leaving `Start()` waiting indefinitely. In addition, `Task.Factory.StartNew` with an async delegate stores an outer task, so `Shutdown()` can return before the accept loop has stopped. Reusing the already-signalled startup event also allows a restart to return before the port is listening.

Bind the TCP listener synchronously so startup errors reach the caller and a successful return means the port is listening. Use `Task.Run` to track the full asynchronous accept loop and capture a cancellation token for each run. Stop the listener in a finally block and dispose its cancellation source after shutdown finishes. This removes the startup event and allows retrying after a failed bind.

Tests cover an occupied port followed by a successful retry, shutdown while a session callback is running, and three start/connect/stop cycles. On the original code, the occupied-port test timed out and the restart test failed with connection refused. After the fix, all three tests pass on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Network.Tests/NexusForever.Network.Tests.csproj
```

`git diff --check` passed. Full-solution builds, Windows, and in-game validation have not been performed. The lifecycle methods retain their existing sequential-caller assumption; concurrent Start/Shutdown calls are not part of this change.

This is independent of #571's socket-close fix. Both PRs introduce the same test-project registration and package versions; either can supply that shared test infrastructure.

open.title: Network: replace APM socket loop and FragmentedBuffer with System.IO.Pipelines
open.head: 1660a4795ea8d6b8ff83408ee53be5b8e0a24772
open.author: xoere2
open.body:
## Summary

- **#477** — Replaces `NetworkSession`'s `BeginReceive`/`EndReceive` APM pattern (and the manual 4096-byte buffer with offset tracking) with `PipeReader.Create(new NetworkStream(socket))`. A background `Task` drives the read loop using `await pipeReader.ReadAsync()`. `OnData` signature changes from `byte[] → uint` (unconsumed byte count) to `ReadOnlySequence<byte> → SequencePosition` so subclasses communicate consumed position back to the pipe.
- **#478** — Deletes `FragmentedBuffer.cs`. `GameSession.OnData` now uses `SequenceReader<byte>`: reads the 4-byte little-endian size prefix, checks if the full payload is available, rewinds and returns early if not. The `PipeReader` redelivers unadvanced bytes on the next read — no manual accumulation needed.
- `StsSession.OnData` adapted to the new signature: materialises the buffer to `byte[]` (required for in-place Arc4 decryption), runs existing `FragmentedStsPacket` logic unchanged, returns `buffer.End`.

## Lifecycle

`OnDisconnect` cancels the `CancellationTokenSource` before closing the socket, so the background read task exits via `OperationCanceledException` rather than a socket exception. `ForceDisconnect` is still called from the `finally` block of the read loop to cover the remote-close case.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build passes with 0 errors
- [ ] Auth flow: client connects, `ClientHelloAuth` dispatched correctly
- [ ] World flow: character select and world entry work end-to-end
- [ ] Fragmented packet: large packet split across multiple TCP segments reassembles correctly
- [ ] Clean disconnect: client close and server-initiated disconnect both exit the read loop without error logs

Closes #477
Closes #478

Note on MailManager updates: 
- Updated `EnqueueMail()` to only push to `pendingMail` Queue. All Mail should be processed by the Update method (which wasn't being called before) otherwise pendingMail won't get moved to availableMail and the Player won't get notified.
- `1000d` -> `1d` change on the `UpdateTimer`. `1000d` is 1000 seconds for the `UpdateTimer`, and the comment mentioned 1 second. So fixed the typo.

This only happens when the Player's Account is sending a Mail to itself, it must be instantly delivered and must be from a Creature. recent.title: Taxi: discover taxi kiosks and handle taxi flights
recent.head: 19786895e3bb399a95576295916318b4dfc9bbc2
recent.body:
## Summary

The taxi window was empty on game_rework and taking a flight did nothing: no taxi nodes were ever sent, and `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF) had no handler. This PR adds kiosk discovery and the flight handler. The player pays and is teleported to the destination.

This is the taxi part of #599 without the bind point parts it sat on. The rest of the taxi work is split into smaller follow up PRs, each built on this one:

| PR | Branch | What it adds | Needs |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| #608 | `fix/taxi-fares` | The fare the taxi map shows, no purchase in combat or without the credits | this PR |
| #609 | `fix/taxi-ride` | The holo cab ride along the route's splines, no casts or attacks on a rider, the landing line | #608 |

## Cause

The taxi map only offers routes through nodes the server says the character discovered, and the server never sent any. Taking a flight or shuttle sends `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF), which had no handler.

## Change

Kiosk nodes are discovered when the player comes within 30 units of a kiosk creature (`Creature2.taxiNodeId`) or talks to it, saved in a new `character_taxi_node` table (with migration), sent with `ServerTaxiNodeUnlock` (0x0186) when found and in `ServerFlightPathUpdate` (0x0188) at login. The flight handler reads the route as TaxiRoute ids, checks that the legs chain from a kiosk near the player and are neutral or of the player's faction, charges the sum of `TaxiRoute.price` and teleports the player to the last leg's node. #608 replaces that price with the one the map shows.

## Migration

This adds the `CharacterTaxiNode` migration and changes `CharacterContextModelSnapshot.cs`. #601 also adds one (`CharacterBind`). Each PR builds and applies on its own against game_rework, but if both merge, the second one needs its migration and snapshot rebased on the first. I can do that once the first one is in.

In #599 this migration came after the bind one. Here its Designer file is the game_rework model plus the taxi node table only. Most of the diff is that generated Designer file (3,039 lines); the rest is about 420 lines.

## Testing

Server only, as in #599. The branch is based on the current game_rework (1f643f63) and the full solution builds in Release with 0 errors and no new warnings. It has not been run in a client on game_rework.

AI (Claude) helped write these changes.

recent.title: Galactic Archive: unlock articles from achievements and quests
recent.head: e41fb57514cc202425430684e11e5fdd8f1b71f0
recent.body:
Gets the Galactic Archive working. Articles and their entries unlock from `ArchiveEntryUnlockRule` when an achievement is completed or a quest is handed in, the state is saved per character, and the client gets every article back after a world change.

Builds on #587 (article id width), so that commit shows here until it's merged.

- `GlobalGalacticArchiveManager` builds the rule index at start-up: for each achievement or quest, which entry slots in which articles it opens. An entry can sit in more than one article, so one rule can open slots in several. 847 of the 867 rules are used; the other 20 point at entries that aren't in any article and get skipped (counted in the start-up log line).
- `GalacticArchiveManager` on the player holds the articles, saved to a new `character_archive_article` table (migration included). The two flag words are stored as the client uses them.
- Hooked in at the end of `QuestManager.QuestComplete` and `CharacterAchievementManager.CompleteAchievement`. A quest counts once it's handed in, not when it's achieved.
- Handlers for `ClientGalacticArchiveUnlock` and `ClientGalacticArchiveViewed`. The client applies both locally before sending them, so the server records them and sends nothing back.
- Every stored article is sent again after each world entry, since the client drops the whole archive on a world change.
- An article's title reward (`characterTitleIdReward`) is granted once every entry in it is unlocked.
- `[GameData]` on `ArchiveArticle`, `ArchiveEntry` and `ArchiveEntryUnlockRule`.

Not covered: path mission rules are loaded but nothing completes a path mission on `game_rework` yet, so they never fire. There's no backfill either, so a character only picks up articles from completions after this lands.

Tested on a local server. Granted every achievement that unlocks something (180) and compared each saved article against what the rule table predicts: 134 articles, all match. Quest unlocks checked with two hand-ins, and an article opened in the panel stays read across world changes. The title reward is the one piece I couldn't reach in testing: only two articles carry one, and nothing I could trigger completes either of them.

recent.title: Fix exception when activating a datacube the character already has
recent.head: f88b196f11b909b4e0db94db2affff3c585d971f
recent.body:
## What was broken

Using a datacube (a lore object whose creature has `DatacubeId` set) works the first time. Using it again, or using another copy of the same datacube, throws `ArgumentException: An item with the same key has already been added` in the world server. The packet handler catches and logs the error, but the player gets nothing back, so the datacube does not play again the way it does after a normal first use.

## Cause

`SimpleEntity.OnActivate` always calls `DatacubeManager.AddDatacube` when the creature has a datacube. `AddDatacube` creates a new entry and adds it with `Dictionary.Add`, which throws when the character already has that datacube. `OnActivateCast` in the same class already checks `GetDatacube` first and only adds when it is missing; `OnActivate` did not.

## Fix

`OnActivate` now looks the datacube up first. If the character does not have it, it is added as before (full progress). If the character already has it, the existing entry is sent to the client again with `SendDatacube`, which matches what `OnActivateCast` does for known datacubes and lets the client show or play it again. Nothing changes for a datacube used for the first time.

## How it was tested

* Full solution build (`dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx -t:Rebuild`): 0 errors, and the same 7 warnings as `game_rework` before the change (no new warnings).
* There is no test project in the solution. I checked the code path by reading it: `ClientActivateUnitHandler` calls `OnActivate`, which calls `AddDatacube`, which calls `Dictionary.Add` with no existence check. `OnActivateCast` in the same class already guards against this.

AI tools (Claude) helped find this bug and write the fix; I reviewed and tested the change.

recent.title: Travel: bind points, recalls, taxis, riding licences, instance return and mounts
recent.head: 38f8c19409c6fc9c3afc08744ce49cb6ed0de1db
recent.body:
## Summary

Most ways of getting around the world did nothing on game_rework. Transmat terminals could not bind a character, so the client hid Recall Transmat. The recall spells were refused by two prerequisite types that had no check. Recall House had no effect handler. The taxi window was empty and taking a flight had no handler. The riding licences were used up without changing mount speed. A dungeon entered through a portal threw when the player was removed, and the Leave button did nothing. A few quick mount summons each spawned a mount.

This PR fixes those in eight commits, one per area. Each commit is self contained and builds on its own, so the commits can be reviewed or cherry picked separately. The prerequisite commit comes first because the recall commits depend on it.

## Areas

| Area | Broken upstream | What this PR changes | Tested |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bind point | `ClientCastBindPointSpell` (0x0098) had no handler, so a character could never bind and the client never learned a bind point | Handler binds to the terminal's BindPoint, new `character_bind` table, `ServerBindPointSet` (0x016D) on change, `ServerPlayerCreate.BindPointId` at login | In game |
| Recall Transmat | Prerequisite types 269 and 204 had no check, so every recall was refused with PrereqCasterCast. A Teleport effect without a location was ignored. Nothing taught spell 8568 | Checks for 269 UnhealthyTime and 204 Dueling, a Teleport without a location goes to the bind point, 8568 granted at login, stuck window bind option casts 49881 | In game |
| Recall House | HousingTeleport had no handler and nothing taught Recall House | HousingTeleport handler sends the player to their residence entrance, Recall House granted to residence owners, stuck window house option casts 49882 | Server only |
| Transmats and Rapid Transport | Refused by the same missing prerequisite checks as the recalls | Fixed by the prerequisite commit | Server only |
| Taxis | No taxi nodes were ever sent, so the taxi window was empty, and `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF) had no handler | Kiosk discovery by proximity or interaction, new `character_taxi_node` table, `ServerTaxiNodeUnlock` (0x0186) and `ServerFlightPathUpdate` (0x0188), flight handler that validates the route, charges the price and teleports | Server only |
| Portals into instances | A dungeon entered through a portal or a teleport has no Match, so the return location was null and removal or unload threw | The player remembers where they left the open world, instances return them there or else to the bind point, removal skips a player with no return location | Server only |
| Celestion and Everstar Grove portals | These only carry an Activate effect | Not included. The fix in our fork builds on an activate spell teleport table that game_rework does not have | Not included |
| Leave buttons | `ClientLeavePendingRemovalInstance` (0x057C) had no handler, and leaving a group inside its dungeon never started a removal | Leave removes the player at once, leaving the group inside a group or raid instance starts the removal warning | Server only |
| Zone transfers | Nothing found broken | No change needed | No change needed |
| Same map teleports | game_rework moves players on the same map through `TeleportTo`, the GM teleport commands included | No change. Our fork's fix depends on a `TeleportToLocal` that game_rework does not have | No change needed |
| Mount summon | Quick casts of a mount spell each spawned a mount, because `CanMount()` only checks `PlatformGuid`, which is set once the player is seated | `SetPendingMount` makes `CanMount()` refuse while the summoned mount is not on the map yet, with a 10 second limit | Server only |
| Mount speed (Riding License 52539, Mount Sprint 80530) | The global cooldown check ignored `UserInitiatedSpellCast`, so after an instant summon such as the Data Drifter (87227) the summon's own global cooldown refused Riding License | The global cooldown check applies to casts the player starts, the summon passes `UserInitiatedSpellCast = false` explicitly | Server only |
| Dismount | `Dismount` did nothing when the vehicle was gone or no longer carried the player, which left the player counted as mounted, and the client will not resurrect a mounted player | `Dismount` clears the platform and gives the player back control | Server only |
| Mount auras on dismount | Riding License and Mount Sprint buff icons are never removed | Not included. game_rework spells finish as soon as their effects run and no buff removal is sent, so this needs aura lifetime support first | Not included |
| Riding skill | The Advanced and Expert Riding Licenses use AddSpell and Disembark effects, which had no handlers, so the licence was used up and speed did not change | AddSpell teaches the spell and casts passive property modifier spells, passives 75441 and 75442 are cast again at login, Disembark dismounts | Server only |
| Mount vendors | Buying and using a mount item goes through the UnlockMount handler that game_rework already has | No change needed | No change needed |
| Rented mounts | The rental licences (77503, 77357, 80223) carry a duration that UnlockMount ignores, so a rental unlocks the mount for good | Not included, needs spell expiry support | Not included |
| Hoverboards | Summoned through the same SummonMount handler as mounts | Covered by the mount summon and dismount changes | Server only |

## Commits

### 1. Prerequisite checks for the recalls (`79ecbcd3`)

Cause: every recall spell has caster cast prerequisite 37806 (type 269), and the stuck window recalls also need 30178 (type 204) through 37809. Neither type had a check, and an unhandled type fails, so Recall Transmat, Recall House, the capital teleports, Rapid Transport and the stuck window recalls were refused with PrereqCasterCast.

Change: `PrerequisiteCheckUnhealthyTime` and `PrerequisiteCheckDueling`. Neither state exists on the server, so NotEqual passes and Equal fails.

Testing: in game as part of Recall Transmat.

### 2. Bind at transmat terminals (`e8dd7c84`)

Cause: using a transmat terminal sends `ClientCastBindPointSpell` (0x0098), which had no handler. A character could never bind, and without a bind point the client hides Recall Transmat.

Change: `ClientCastBindPointSpellHandler` binds the player to the terminal's BindPoint. The bind point is stored in a new `character_bind` table (with migration), sent with `ServerBindPointSet` (0x016D) when it changes and in `ServerPlayerCreate` (the former `UnknownBC`, now `BindPointId`) at login.

Testing: in game.

### 3. Recall Transmat (`5d5059b8`)

Cause: Recall Transmat (8568) and the stuck window recall (49881) use a Teleport effect without a WorldLocation2 id, which the handler ignored. The only reward that taught 8568 was from quest 4891, which is no longer in the tables. The stuck window (`ClientStuck`) had no handler.

Change: a Teleport without a location sends the player to their bind point. Every character is given Recall Transmat at login. `ClientStuckHandler` casts 49881 for the bind point option.

Testing: in game.

### 4. Recall House (`15137ba7`)

Cause: Recall House (38408) and the stuck window recall (49882) use a HousingTeleport effect, which had no handler, and nothing taught the spell.

Change: HousingTeleport handler that sends the player to their residence entrance the same way the housing return button does. Recall House (base 22919) is given to every residence owner. The stuck window's house option casts 49882.

Testing: server only.

### 5. Taxis (`cbda9364`)

Cause: the taxi map only offers routes through nodes the server says the character discovered, and the server never sent any. Taking a flight or shuttle sends `ClientTaxiFlight` (0x00FF), which had no handler.

Change: kiosk nodes are discovered when the player comes within 30 units of a kiosk creature (`Creature2.taxiNodeId`) or talks to it, saved in a new `character_taxi_node` table (with migration), sent with `ServerTaxiNodeUnlock` (0x0186) when found and in `ServerFlightPathUpdate` (0x0188) at login. The flight handler reads the route as TaxiRoute ids, checks that the legs chain from a kiosk near the player and are neutral or of the player's faction, charges the sum of `TaxiRoute.price` and teleports the player to the last leg's node.

Testing: server only.

### 6. Riding licences (`4b46e1ea`)

Cause: the Advanced and Expert Riding Licenses (items 49296 and 49297, spells 60333 and 60338) teach the Riding Skill passives 75441 and 75442 through an AddSpell effect and end with a Disembark effect. Neither effect had a handler, so the licence was used up and mount speed did not change.

Change: AddSpell teaches the spell and casts it when it is a passive made only of UnitPropertyModifier effects. Those passives are cast again at login, since property modifiers are not saved. Disembark dismounts the player.

Testing: server only.

### 7. Instance return and the Leave button (`9d5c922c`)

Cause: a dungeon entered through a portal or a teleport has no Match, so `ContentMapInstance.GetPlayerReturnLocation` returned null, and a pending removal or an unload then called `TeleportTo(null)` and threw. The Leave button on the removal warning sends `ClientLeavePendingRemovalInstance` (0x057C), which had no handler, and leaving a group inside its dungeon never started a removal.

Change: the player remembers where they left the open world, and an instance returns them there, else to their bind point. Removal and unload skip a player with no return location instead of throwing. The Leave button removes the player at once, and leaving the group inside a group or raid instance starts the removal warning. Both run on the map update through a queue, since they arrive from outside it.

Testing: server only.

### 8. Mounts (`38f8c194`)

Cause: the map adds a summoned mount on its next update and `PlatformGuid` is only set once the player is seated, so `CanMount()` let every quick summon cast through and each one spawned a mount. The global cooldown check in `Spell.CheckCast` ignored `UserInitiatedSpellCast`, so after an instant summon such as the Data Drifter (87227) the Riding License cast (52539) was refused by the global cooldown the summon had just started. `Dismount` did nothing when the vehicle was gone or no longer carried the player, which left `PlatformGuid` set, and a dead player still counted as mounted.

Change: `Player.SetPendingMount` makes `CanMount()` refuse while the summoned mount is not on the map yet, for at most 10 seconds. The global cooldown check only applies to casts the player starts, and the summon passes `UserInitiatedSpellCast = false` for Riding License and Mount Sprint. `Dismount` clears a platform whose vehicle is gone and gives the player back control.

Testing: server only.

## Testing

Bind and Recall Transmat were tested in game on 25 October 2026. Everything else is server side only: every commit builds the WorldServer project on its own, and the full solution builds in Release at the tip with 0 errors. game_rework has no test project to run.

AI (Claude) helped write these changes, and I reviewed them.

recent.title: Fix server dirty character jobs never ending when a character is marked dirty again during a run
recent.head: 8ca89ccb31c20a286a64ac632fca8885d812cba5
recent.body:
## What was broken

`CharacterDirtyRealmScheduledJob` and `CharacterDirtyStatsScheduledJob` in the group server can get stuck in a busy loop that never finishes. While stuck, the job keeps picking the same character, publishes the same stale update over and over, never clears the flag, and never reaches any other dirty character. Because both jobs are `[DisallowConcurrentExecution]`, the run never ends and later runs never start, so realm and stats updates for the other group members stop going out.

## Cause

Each job uses one injected `GroupContext` for the whole run and loops on `CharacterRepository.GetNextCharacterWithDirtyRealm()` (or `...DirtyStats()`). The query is a tracking query, so once a character has been loaded in that context, later queries return the instance that is already tracked and do not refresh its values.

The sequence that triggers it:

1. The job loads character A, sets `RealmDirty = false` and saves.
2. A message handler in another scope (for example `PlayerWorldUpdatedHandler` or `PlayerWorldZoneUpdatedHandler`) sets `RealmDirty = true` for A again in the database.
3. The next query in the job matches A in the database, but returns the tracked instance, which still says `RealmDirty = false`.
4. The job sets it to false again. EF sees no change, `SaveChangesAsync` writes nothing, and the database still says dirty.
5. The next query returns A again, forever.

The stats job is the most exposed, since stats change often and it runs every 2 seconds. The group and member lookups inside the loop also load other characters into the same context, so any of them can end up stale the same way.

## Fix

Each character is now processed in its own DI scope created from `IServiceScopeFactory`. The repository, `GroupContext`, `IInternalMessagePublisher` and the `Character` are resolved from that scope, so every iteration starts with a fresh context and reads the current database values. The publisher and the context come from the same scope, so outbox messages are still saved together with the flag change. The rest of the job logic is unchanged.

## How it was tested

* Full solution build (`dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx -t:Rebuild`): 0 errors, and the same 7 warnings as `game_rework` before the change (no new warnings).
* There is no test project in the solution, so I wrote a small throwaway console harness (not part of this PR) that references the group server, uses the EF Core InMemory provider, seeds two dirty characters, and marks the first one dirty again from a separate context right after the job's first save. The job was given a 3 second cancellation token.
  * Before the fix: both jobs ran until cancelled, about 20,000 (realm) and 30,000 (stats) `SaveChanges` calls in 3 seconds, and both characters were still dirty at the end. The second character was never processed.
  * After the fix: both jobs returned on their own in about 350 ms with 3 saves, and no character was left dirty.
* We also saw this on a live server: the realm job resent the same stale realm update to the client about 35 times a second, most characters stayed realm dirty, and other group server work queued behind it.

AI tools (Claude) helped find this bug and write the fix and the test harness; I reviewed and tested the change.

recent.title: implement SpellEffect 73 ModifySpellCooldown
recent.head: e100f4c29a1571a7181d06967ed8133612d99074
recent.body:
# Implement spell effect type 73 (ModifySpellCooldown)

Base: `expedition-evil-from-the-ether`. Independent of the heal work.

## Why

Type 73 is the most common spell effect type the server does not handle: 522 `Spell4Effects` rows on 467 spells, 382 of them class abilities. Without a handler those effects are silently ignored, so cooldown resets and reductions (Recharge, Onslaught, AMP cooldown reductions, ...) do nothing.

## What the effect does

Each row has four fields:

| field | meaning |
|---|---|
| `dataBits00` scope | which cooldowns it matches: 0 = base spell id, 1 = `Spell4` id, 2 = spell group id, 3 = `SpellCoolDown` id |
| `dataBits01` key | the id to match in that key space |
| `dataBits02` mode | 0 = multiply, can only shorten; 1 = multiply, unclamped; 2 = add milliseconds (negative = reduce), floored at 0; 3 = set to an absolute number of milliseconds |
| `dataBits03` magnitude | float; milliseconds for modes 2 and 3, a factor for modes 0 and 1 |

Two things happen when the effect lands:

1. Every matching cooldown that is **running** is re-armed from its remaining time. A spell that is not on cooldown is not given one.
2. If the effect has a lifetime (`CancelOnly`, or delay + duration > 0: 85 of the 522 rows), the modifier is **held** and applied to every cooldown that starts while it is held, in the order the records were added. Removing it does not restore a cooldown it already shortened. The other 437 rows are one-shot.

## Implementation

- New handler, data class and the two enums (scope, mode) for `SpellEffectType.ModifySpellCooldown` (the enum member already existed).
- The arithmetic is shared with the existing `SetSpellCooldownByBaseSpell`, whose `type` parameter turned out to be this mode field.
- A per-player list of held records, folded into new cooldowns server-side so the server's own timer is authoritative.

### What is sent to the client

The client applies its own copy of the modifier to the duration of any cooldown node it has to create, so a reduction already folded in by the server would be applied twice. A new cooldown is therefore **sent with the duration before the server's own fold** and **stored with the folded value**. The one-shot re-arm sends nothing, because the client performs the same re-arm itself when the effect arrives.

## Bug fixes this needed

These are in cooldown code this feature is the first caller of:

1. The cooldown setters threw on a negative value. All 145 mode-2 magnitudes are negative, so the value is now floored at 0.
2. `SetSpellCooldown` threw when the `Spell4` row or base info was missing. 7 shipped rows name a missing `Spell4Base` id and 16 rows have key 0; both now mean "nothing matches".
3. `SetSpellCooldownByGroupId` threw if any unrelated spell in the dictionary had a missing row. It skips such entries now.
4. `SetSpellCooldownByGroupId` and `SetSpellCooldownByBaseSpell` could not emit `ServerCooldown`. Both take an `emit` argument now.
5. `ISpellInfo.Cooldowns` can contain `null`; guarded.

## Second commit: send the cooldown node types the client has

`ServerCooldown` carries a type, and the client keeps one cooldown node per (type, key). The server only ever sent type 1 (per spell). That left two gaps:

| type | what it is | key | what the server did |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | global cooldown | `Spell4.spellCoolDownIdGlobal` | tracked server-side, never sent |
| 1 | per-spell cooldown | `Spell4` id | sent |
| 2 | cooldown shared by every spell with the same `SpellCoolDown` id | `SpellCoolDown` id | tracked server-side, never sent |

So sibling spells that share a cooldown showed no cooldown on the action bar, and `Property.CooldownReductionModifier` (136) was declared but never read. The client does not apply that property to a duration the server sends, so if the server doesn't, nothing does.

This commit:

1. Emits a type 2 node for every `SpellCoolDown` id a spell carries, mirroring the client's own sender.
2. Gives a shared cooldown the duration the client gives it, `SpellCoolDown.cooldownTime`, falling back to the spell's own cooldown when the row has none.
3. Applies `CooldownReductionModifier` to the cooldown the server starts, for spells tagged Assault, Support or Utility, with the client's truncation to whole milliseconds. The property defaults to 1.0, so nothing changes unless something modifies it. A value of zero or less is treated as "no modifier".
4. Emits a type 0 node for the global cooldown (including the reset when a cast is cancelled by movement). The server's own dictionary stays keyed by `globalCooldownEnum`; only the wire value changes.

**Behaviour change to be aware of:** `cooldownIds` is read by `Spell.CheckCast`, so a shared cooldown whose `SpellCoolDown` row is longer or shorter than the spell's own cooldown now gates casting differently. This matches the client, but it affects every spell with a shared cooldown id (about 2,900 `Spell4` rows).

The client never shortens a running type-0 node, so a global cooldown sent shorter than the one already running is ignored by the client.

`CooldownReductionModifier` has no base value of its own in this server: it falls through `CalculateDefaultProperty` to the `CreatureLevel` table, where it happens to land on a column holding 1.0. Worth a separate issue.

tested **In game** (cast through the command system, because tiering up spells in the limited action set is not implemented; the cooldown node changes were applied during the test): The cooldowns that were running were modified and the times shown in the client matched the expected values exactly.

## Known limits

- The client's `max(delay, duration)` special case (one spell flag) is not modelled; it changes no row's held/one-shot classification.
- Casting the same spell again appends a second record, as the client does.
- A scope-2 record is a broadcast (group 475 covers 201 spells); only running cooldowns are touched.
- Six scope-2 mode-3 rows cannot start a cooldown, only shorten a running one, as in the client.
