recent.title: Clear an entity's own vision collections when it is removed from a map
recent.head: f9e067f49c60169af136dcf8d04acc87e55d3fd7
recent.body:
`GridEntity.OnRemoveFromMap` loops over `visibleEntities` and `invisibleEntities` and calls `RemoveVisionEntity(this)` for each entry, which removes the entity from its own collections once but leaves every other entry in place. Players keep their instance when they move between maps, so they carry stale entries keyed by guids of the previous map.

On the new map `UpdateVision` skips guids that are already in the collections. Any entity that happens to get a guid from that stale list is never sent to the client. When that is the player's own guid the client stays on an endless loading screen, and for other entities the client is missing objects (falling through props it never received). Which guids collide depends on the order entities were created, so it shows up randomly after map changes.

The loop now only removes the entity from the other entities' collections, and its own collections are cleared afterwards.

Found while testing repeated map changes into an instance (the problem came in with 801cbc565). Tested on a local server by moving between world 22 and an instance repeatedly: no more endless loading screens or missing objects.

recent.title: NPE quest scripting example: Navigating Nexus → Claim to Stake
recent.head: 7975e0d47ef4b43b493884d0166c04f7370dac2a
recent.body:
## Summary

This PR adds a **playable New Player Experience (world 3460) quest path** from **Navigating Nexus** through **Face of the Enemy** into **A Claim to Stake** (housing hologram).

**Primary goal: example / reference code to inspire more quest progress.**
NexusForever still has huge gaps in quest scripting. This branch is meant as a working pattern others can copy, not a finished NPE or a claim that all quests should look exactly like this. If it helps someone wire their first `TalkTo`, `EnterArea`, CSI, or map hand-off, it did its job.

Use it as inspiration for:

- Other NPE steps (Lots in Store, Bon Voyage, etc.)
- Zone quests elsewhere in the world
- Shared objective wiring (`SucceedCSI`, `EnterArea`, checklist bits, parent `EnterZone`)

## Why this matters

A lot of retail quest data already exists in tables/SQL; what’s missing is **server-side hooks and scripts**. This PR shows one end-to-end slice:

1. Discover quests / objectives (`!quest world`)
2. Wire objective types in core gameplay
3. Add map / quest / entity scripts for the story beats
4. Hand off between quests without fake auto-teleports where retail uses a projector

## Playable flow (Exile; Dominion mirrored)

| Step | Quest | What happens |
|------|--------|----------------|
| 1 | Navigating Nexus (10527 / 10532) | Jump / hoverboard / boosters → combat projector → force-complete + teleport into combat hologram |
| 2 | Face of the Enemy (10518 / 10524) | Combat cinematic → beasts → mines → turrets → legionnaires → force-complete + **grant housing** (player stays put) |
| 3 | A Claim to Stake (10525 / 10526) | Activate **housing hologram projector 73741** → housing plot → Protostar talks (sky/music “upload”) → find Phineas |

**Not in this PR:** Lots in Store! (10540), Bon Voyage, and later NPE.

## Detailed changes

### Core quest objective wiring

- `SucceedCSI` — CSI / activate paths update objectives
- `EnterArea` — from `WorldLocation2` indicators (minimum radius 5; many NPE markers use radius 1)
- `ActivateTargetGroupChecklist` — per-player bitfield slots via `QuestChecklistIdx`
- `EnterZone` — credit **leaf zone and all parents** (e.g. housing plot `5969` → hologram `4965`)
- `!quest world` — diagnostic listing quests tied to a world (default 3460)
- `!quest achieve` — GM-friendly: add if missing, clear sequential objectives, finish Achieved → Completed, chat feedback

### Activate / mount reliability

- Cast creature `Spell4IdActivate*` on activate-cast (hoverboard projector, etc.)
- Skip non-`IUnitEntity` activate targets (SimpleCollidable props crashed spell start)
- Don’t advance quests if activate cast fails; more reliable vehicle boarding

### NPE scripts (`NexusForever.Script.Main/Tutorial`)

- **TutorialMapScript** — auto-grant starter / combat / housing when prerequisites are met
- **NavigatingNexusQuestScript** — barrier despawn, combat hand-off teleport
- **FaceOfTheEnemyQuestScript** — cinematic on accept; on achieve force-complete + grant Claim to Stake (**no** auto-teleport to housing)
- **ClaimToStakeQuestScript** — EnterZone credit only if already inside housing hologram
- Combat AI: battle beasts, holo soldiers, interruptible hostile sim-turrets
- Objective rings, extra boosters, related helpers

### Client / interaction

- **Housing projector `73741`** — activate teleports into housing plot (spell itself is Activate + fullscreen only)
- **`ClientDialogOpened` → `ServerDialogEnd`** — fixes empty TalkTo “Uploading…” hang
- Sky / Music specialists cast NPE skybox / music change spells on TalkTo
- Null-safe `TakeDamage` (stops NRE spam)

## How to treat this as a template

If you’re adding another quest, the useful pieces to copy are:

1. **Wire the objective type once in core** if nothing calls `ObjectiveUpdate` for it yet.
2. Prefer **`[ScriptFilterOwnerId]` / `[ScriptFilterCreatureId]`** scripts over one-off hacks when behavior is content-specific.
3. **Map scripts** for grant / zone enter; **quest scripts** for accept / achieve / hand-off; **entity scripts** for interact / range / AI.
4. Match retail flow when possible (e.g. projector click vs silent teleport).
5. Add a small GM diagnostic when discovery is hard.

Imperfect or NPE-specific shortcuts are fine to leave behind—**the pattern is the point**.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh NPE char: Navigating Nexus completes into combat hologram
- [ ] Face of the Enemy: full combat path (or `!quest achieve 10518`) → grants 10525, **no** housing teleport
- [ ] Activate projector at ~`-176, -848, 626` → housing plot
- [ ] Talk Landscape ×2, Decor ×2, Sky, Music (no Uploading hang) → find Phineas
- [ ] Relog mid-quest does not soft-lock hand-offs
- [ ] Dominion path mirrors (10532 / 10524 / 10526)

## Notes for reviewers

- Target branch: **`game_rework`**.
- Intended as **inspirational / incremental** content for the community, happy to split, rename, or trim NPE-specific bits if that’s easier to land.
- World DB NPE SQL is assumed loaded for entity spawns; scripts bind by creature/quest id.

recent.title: Start public event objective timers on activation, complete TimedWin on expiry
recent.head: 2896190f5f2a32b7e3b972eb32c459c10c6c0f72
recent.body:
`PublicEventObjective` creates its failure timer in `Initialise`, when the public event is created, and `Update` ticks it whatever the objective's status. As discussed on Discord this was never really implemented for any public event, and it causes two bugs:

- An objective activated later in an event has already used up its timer, so it fails as soon as it becomes active (or before).
- The timer keeps running after an objective has succeeded and can then set it to Failed.

Every timed objective also fails when its timer ends. `TimedWin` (13) objectives are won by lasting until the timer ends, so they should succeed instead. The client tables back this up: there are 213 `TimedWin` objectives (210 with a timer), and all of them read that way:
- waits and story lines: "Wait for Vesna Taranoft to inspect the Weapons Skiff", "Listen to Vice-Marshal Dawson's briefing";
- surviving: "Avoid the Artillery Barrage", "Avoid Land Mines", "Hold ...", "Defend ...";
- timed collecting: "Collect as much Food and Water as you can", "Scavenge scrap to repair as many Moisture Collectors as you can".

Changes (`PublicEventObjective.cs`):
- Initial objectives start their elapsed and failure timers in `Initialise`, other objectives when they are activated (also after `ResetObjective`).
- Timers only advance while the objective is Active.
- The failure timer is dropped on any other status change, so a succeeded objective can't fail anymore.
- `ElapsedTimeMs` counts from activation.
- A `TimedWin` objective succeeds when its timer ends, every other timed objective still fails.
- On activation the full objective update is sent instead of the status update. The client runs the countdown from the `ElapsedTimeMs` it last received, so an objective activated later showed a timer that had been running since the event started. Sending both made the countdown flicker; the full update already contains the status.

Tested with the Hycrest Insurrection intro (public event 418) on a local server, without any script completing the objective:
- Objective 2155 "Listen to Vice-Marshal Dawson's briefing" (`TimedWin`, 20 s) is activated about a minute into the event. It stays active for its full 20 s and the tracker counts down from 0:20.
- When the timer ends 2155 succeeds and the event moves on to the next objective.
- Objectives that succeed before their timer ends stay succeeded.

This matches Laughing's description on Discord of a "wait" objective type that should succeed when its timer ends. Survive-type objectives that should fail when the players lose (e.g. everyone dies) would need that failure from the script; the timer itself only completes them.

recent.title: Coalesce movement relocations in the map grid action queue
recent.head: 9289cbb1fdfb0ff06b90f124d2a9760a1d5655ab
recent.body:
Since c8a6d887 removed the relocation timer from the position command group (its message notes this might need to be revisited), every moving entity queues a relocation on every tick. `BaseMap` only processes `GridActionThreshold` (100) grid actions per update, so once a map has more moving entities than that the queue grows faster than it is processed. Every other grid action waits behind the backlog: adding or removing a player could take minutes, and the client gave up on the loading screen.

Movement relocations are now coalesced per entity. `GridEntity.RelocateOnMap` without a caller callback queues its relocation with a coalesce flag: while one is queued for the entity, a new relocation only updates the pending target, and the queued action moves the entity to the latest position when it is processed. Relocations with a caller callback (teleports) are queued as before.

Update: the first version coalesced relocations without a callback, but `RelocateOnMap` always passes the entity's own `OnRelocate`, so it never applied to movement. It now uses an explicit flag.

Tested on a local server with around 170 units walking splines on one map: players are added and removed right away, where before a player's add waited several minutes.

recent.title: Generalise prerequisite evaluation and spell contexts
recent.head: f366375743619958c8d93efcb9d7cee7fb63ac15
recent.body:
## Summary

This updates the prerequisite system to evaluate any `IUnitEntity` and provides explicit target context for relationship-based prerequisite checks.

It also completes the existing spell-level cast, persistence, effect-application, and proc prerequisite paths, while retaining the expedition branch's existing RapidTransport prerequisite validation behavior. No new prerequisite handlers or testing infrastructure are introduced.

## Changes

### Prerequisite evaluation

- Changed `IPrerequisiteCheck` and `IPrerequisiteManager` subjects from `IPlayer` to `IUnitEntity`.
- Added a manager overload accepting a target-context unit.
- Continued using the existing prerequisite-parameter factory for context creation.
- Added `Target`, `TaxiNode`, and nullable `CastResult` prerequisite parameters.
- Preserved the same parameter context through nested prerequisite evaluation.
- Updated existing handlers:
  - Unit-compatible handlers operate directly on `IUnitEntity`.
  - Player-specific handlers explicitly require an `IPlayer`.
  - Existing unimplemented handlers remain pass-through so they do not block spell casts.
- Corrected the native raw comparison mapping:
  - `3` is greater than.
  - `4` is greater than or equal.
  - `5` is less than.
  - `6` is less than or equal.
- Changed unsupported comparison branches in implemented handlers to fail closed.

### Spell prerequisite lifecycle

- Removed the player-only prerequisite bypass.
- Added caster-cast evaluation using `(caster, explicit target)`.
- Added target-cast evaluation using `(explicit target, caster)`.
- Added caster-persistence evaluation using `(caster, explicit target)`.
- Added target-persistence evaluation using `(explicit target, caster)`.
- Reused one explicit-target resolution path for validation, persistence, and execution.
- Missing required targets now fail the appropriate target-stage check or finish the active spell.
- Propagated `TaxiNode` into cast and persistence prerequisite parameters.
- Allowed caster- and target-cast prerequisite handlers to return a specific `CastResult`, with the existing stage-specific result retained as the fallback.

### Effect application

- Completed per-target effect prerequisite evaluation.
- Caster-apply prerequisites use `(caster, affected target)`.
- Target-apply prerequisites use `(affected target, caster)`.
- Removed the earlier context-free caster-apply check.
- Effect prerequisite failure skips application to that target rather than rejecting the entire cast.

### Proc integration

- Proc target prerequisites use `(trigger target, proc owner)`.
- Proc caster prerequisites use `(proc owner, trigger target)`.
- The accepted trigger target GUID is retained across the proc delay.
- Triggered spells receive the original target through `PrimaryTargetId`, preserving the correct context for downstream spell prerequisites.

### Spell metadata naming

Renamed the cached prerequisite properties to match the singular GameTable fields:

- `TargetCastPrerequisite`
- `CasterPersistencePrerequisite`
- `TargetPersistencePrerequisite`

### RapidTransport prerequisite

- Restored the existing `PrerequisiteType.RapidTransport` eligibility and affordability validation.
- Requires a player subject and valid taxi-node context.
- Validates taxi-node availability, auto-unlock level, destination data, minimum distance, and the RapidTransport cooldown formula.
- Uses the existing `IRapidTransportCostCalculator` and currency managers to check service-token or credit affordability.
- Returns `ServiceTokensInsufficentFunds` or `CasterVitalCostMoney` for the corresponding insufficient-funds cases, with `RapidTransportInvalid` as the general failure result.

This restores the expedition branch's server behavior; it does not claim that prerequisite type 269's client semantics have been confirmed by reverse engineering.

## Compatibility notes

- `Target` is the contextual counterpart to the evaluated `subject`; for target-side checks it therefore contains the caster.
- Runner overrides remain limited to the existing caster-cast stage.
- Cast-time target prerequisites apply only to the explicit target.
- Implicit AoE candidates are not evaluated with `TargetCastPrerequisite`.
- Unknown prerequisite types without a registered handler retain the manager's existing behavior.
- This does not implement new prerequisite handlers.

## Out of scope

- AoE target and preferred-target prerequisites.
- Effect persistence and target-suspend prerequisites.
- New test projects or prerequisite test infrastructure.
- Further interpretation of prerequisite type 269 beyond restoring the existing server behavior.

## Validation

- `dotnet build Source/NexusForever.slnx --no-restore --nologo --verbosity:minimal`
- Build completed with 0 errors.
- The existing 127 warnings remain.
- `git diff --check` passes.
- No tests were added or modified.

recent.title: Allow client side interaction spells on entities that aren't units
recent.head: 8fef69be625e682e78a8bc4fb8a30735bb0d1ebd
recent.body:

recent.title: Fix players standing on platform entities
recent.head: ce327232b3ce4f3c8ff360ffa135e6dafb4ff458
recent.body:
Three problems found with players standing on a spawned platform entity (a moving ship the players ride on). They are separate changes, happy to split them into their own PRs if preferred.

**Dismount throws on a non-vehicle platform.** `Player.Dismount` does `GetVisible<IVehicleEntity>(PlatformGuid)`. The platform can also be a normal entity the player stands on, so every user-initiated spell cast while standing on one threw `InvalidCastException`. It now only removes the passenger when the platform is a vehicle.

**Teleports keep the platform.** `OnTeleportToLocal` broadcasts the new position while the player is still attached to the platform. The client takes it as an offset from the platform and puts the player far outside the map (an empty void). A world change (`TeleportTo`) also kept the old map's platform guid. Both now call `SetPlatform(null)` first.

**Platform rotation ignored.** `PositionCommandGroup.Relocate` adds the platform position to the player's platform-relative position, but that position is in the platform's own turned frame. On a platform turned by -90° a player standing next to an NPC on it was placed 26.5 m away on the grid and could not interact with it. The relative position is now rotated by the platform's yaw (`Rotation.X`) before the platform position is added:

```
world = (x cos r + z sin r, y, -x sin r + z cos r) + platform position
```

Tested on a local server with a platform entity turned -90°: interaction range with NPCs on the platform is correct (checked against measured positions), casting spells on the platform no longer throws, and teleporting off the platform lands at the target position. Also tested with the platform flying (position keys) and turning 90° (rotation keys) with players and NPCs attached as passengers (`SetPlatform`): they stay in place on it and their server-side positions follow the platform through the turn.

recent.title: Shared: preserve deferred events when the queue is blocked
recent.head: 12f77cfa61c7e3820fccb9ebc0bcaf639337ab86
recent.body:
Fixes #420.

When EventQueue.Update encounters an unready blocking event, it currently returns before re-enqueueing standard events deferred earlier in the tick. Those events are silently lost. Stop the processing loop instead, allowing the existing requeue step to run. Standard events still move to the back of the queue, and the blocking event continues to prevent subsequent execution until ready.

Add a Shared test project with four cases covering one or multiple deferred events, repeated blocked ticks, preserved execution order and exactly-once execution, an event that becomes ready after the blocker completes, and the existing non-blocking behavior of standard events.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Shared.Tests/NexusForever.Shared.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

Before the fix: 3 failures, 1 pass. After the fix: all 4 cases pass. `git diff --check` also passes. Full-solution, Windows, and in-game validation were not performed.

This is independent of #571, #572, and #573. It uses the same central test package versions and adds a Shared test project; when integrating those PRs, retain both test projects in the solution's Tests folder.

recent.title: Network: close the socket even when shutdown fails
recent.head: c29b95a7ad3cbdee7594b5b31aaf767d82b46abe
recent.body:
`NetworkSession.OnDisconnect` currently calls `Shutdown` and `Close` in the same try block. If endpoint lookup or shutdown throws, the catch logs the exception and the session is marked complete without closing its socket. Move `Close` into a finally block so the session releases its socket on that error path too.

Add a small xUnit test project to the solution. Loopback tests cover connected and already-disconnected sockets, session completion, and repeated disconnect requests. A focused regression test injects an unconnected socket through reflection to exercise the shutdown exception path without receive callbacks changing the socket state; it fails on the original code because the handle remains open. This is an isolated error-path test, not a claim that an ordinary peer disconnect causes the exception.

Validation: `dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Network.Tests/NexusForever.Network.Tests.csproj` on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401: all 3 tests passed. The original code failed the handle-closure assertion in the isolated error-path test; the two loopback cases already passed. `git diff --check` also passed. Full solution, Windows, and in-game validation are not covered.

Related work: open PR #566 changes the receive loop but retains the same shutdown/close sequence. This patch is limited to socket cleanup and introduces no receive-loop changes.

recent.title: GameTable: allow retry after cache initialization fails
recent.head: ac913c09cd8bce2fdbcf1839fd33ea9c5662b794
recent.body:
If cache preparation throws after CheckAndCleanupCache claims the initialization flag, cacheCheck remains 1. Every subsequent LoadWithCache call then stays in the polling loop, even after the filesystem problem has been repaired.

Reset the flag to 0 when cache preparation fails and rethrow the original exception. This allows a later or waiting caller to retry while preserving the existing successful initialization and cache invalidation behavior.

Add four GameTable test cases: recovery after a file blocks creation of the cache directory, recovery after a directory blocks writing cacheInfo.txt, deletion of stale cache files, and preservation of files with a matching module version. Recovery cases also verify that the creator was not invoked on failed preparation and that a subsequent load uses the newly written cache entry. Tests isolate process-wide state and release the old implementation's blocked worker after the timeout assertion, so failed regression tests do not hang the suite.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal
```

Before the fix: 2 recovery cases time out, 2 normal cases pass. After the fix: all 4 cases pass. `git diff --check` passes. Full-solution, Windows, in-game testing, and a concurrent stress test were not performed.

The current GameTableFactory cache call is commented out. This fixes the FileCache API; it does not claim an observed failure in the current default server startup or gameplay path. It does not enable the cache or change concurrent writes to individual cache entries.


Independent of #571–#575. Shares the GameTable test project and central package versions with #575. When combining them, keep both FileCacheTests.cs and WideStringTests.cs, with one project entry and one set of central package entries.

recent.title: GameTable: read supplementary Unicode characters in wide strings
recent.head: ac10142e60b6587b27b73da07ef9d4448f09a3af
recent.body:
ReadWideString currently calls BinaryReader.ReadChar with UTF-16 encoding. Valid supplementary Unicode characters require a surrogate pair, but ReadChar supplies space for only one char. Reading such a character throws ArgumentException (output char buffer too small), including through StringTable.GetEntry.

Read UTF-16LE code units up to the null terminator and decode the complete byte sequence together. This preserves surrogate pairs, remains independent of the caller's BinaryReader encoding, and leaves bytes after the terminator available to the caller. Missing or truncated terminators still throw EndOfStreamException.

Add a GameTable test project with nine cases covering empty strings, ASCII, BMP Unicode, supplementary characters alone and mixed with other characters, StringTable offset lookups, following-byte preservation, and missing or truncated terminators.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests/NexusForever.GameTable.Tests.csproj --no-restore --verbosity minimal
```

Before the fix: 3 failures, 6 passes. After the fix: all 9 cases pass. `git diff --check` passes. Full-solution, Windows, and in-game validation were not performed. The regression is demonstrated with synthetic valid UTF-16 input; no claim is made that existing client data contains these characters.


Independent of #571–#574. Uses the same central test package versions; when combining these PRs, retain all test projects in the solution's Tests folder.

recent.title: Network: reject reads past the end of a game packet
recent.head: 00f8876ffa6ac239a7b98db153d9fd1c6a81734e
recent.body:
`GamePacketReader.ReadBit()` casts `Stream.ReadByte()` directly to byte. At end of stream, the returned -1 becomes 0xFF, so truncated fields silently acquire set bits instead of reporting missing input. For example, reading a UInt32 from an empty stream currently produces UInt32.MaxValue.

Check the stream result before converting it and throw `EndOfStreamException` when no byte is available. Update the cached byte and bit position only after a successful refill, so repeated reads after EOF cannot expose stale bits. Valid bit order, cross-byte fields, padding resets, seeking, and zero-length reads are preserved.

Validation on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Network.Tests/NexusForever.Network.Tests.csproj --no-restore
```

Before the fix: 8 failures and 2 passes. After the fix: all 10 tests pass. The tests cover empty/exhausted streams, repeated EOF reads, truncated integers and strings, valid cross-byte fields, reset/seek behavior, and zero-length reads. `git diff --check` also passes.

The existing GameSession exception handler catches read failures before dispatching the message handler; this change does not add a disconnect policy. Full-solution builds, Windows, and in-game validation have not been performed. In-game validation should check whether any existing message definitions read beyond their actual payload, since such reads now fail explicitly.

This is independent of the functional changes in #571 and #572 and uses the same test-project registration and package versions.

recent.title: Network: make listener startup and shutdown reliable
recent.head: 39012c403e3d2fcdf0d9f7947c14c95ba5fd9c16
recent.body:
Starting a listener on an occupied port currently faults the background task before it signals the startup event, leaving `Start()` waiting indefinitely. In addition, `Task.Factory.StartNew` with an async delegate stores an outer task, so `Shutdown()` can return before the accept loop has stopped. Reusing the already-signalled startup event also allows a restart to return before the port is listening.

Bind the TCP listener synchronously so startup errors reach the caller and a successful return means the port is listening. Use `Task.Run` to track the full asynchronous accept loop and capture a cancellation token for each run. Stop the listener in a finally block and dispose its cancellation source after shutdown finishes. This removes the startup event and allows retrying after a failed bind.

Tests cover an occupied port followed by a successful retry, shutdown while a session callback is running, and three start/connect/stop cycles. On the original code, the occupied-port test timed out and the restart test failed with connection refused. After the fix, all three tests pass on Linux with .NET SDK 10.0.401:

```sh
dotnet test Source/NexusForever.Network.Tests/NexusForever.Network.Tests.csproj
```

`git diff --check` passed. Full-solution builds, Windows, and in-game validation have not been performed. The lifecycle methods retain their existing sequential-caller assumption; concurrent Start/Shutdown calls are not part of this change.

This is independent of #571's socket-close fix. Both PRs introduce the same test-project registration and package versions; either can supply that shared test infrastructure.

recent.title: Network: replace APM socket loop and FragmentedBuffer with System.IO.Pipelines
recent.head: 1660a4795ea8d6b8ff83408ee53be5b8e0a24772
recent.body:
## Summary

- **#477** — Replaces `NetworkSession`'s `BeginReceive`/`EndReceive` APM pattern (and the manual 4096-byte buffer with offset tracking) with `PipeReader.Create(new NetworkStream(socket))`. A background `Task` drives the read loop using `await pipeReader.ReadAsync()`. `OnData` signature changes from `byte[] → uint` (unconsumed byte count) to `ReadOnlySequence<byte> → SequencePosition` so subclasses communicate consumed position back to the pipe.
- **#478** — Deletes `FragmentedBuffer.cs`. `GameSession.OnData` now uses `SequenceReader<byte>`: reads the 4-byte little-endian size prefix, checks if the full payload is available, rewinds and returns early if not. The `PipeReader` redelivers unadvanced bytes on the next read — no manual accumulation needed.
- `StsSession.OnData` adapted to the new signature: materialises the buffer to `byte[]` (required for in-place Arc4 decryption), runs existing `FragmentedStsPacket` logic unchanged, returns `buffer.End`.

## Lifecycle

`OnDisconnect` cancels the `CancellationTokenSource` before closing the socket, so the background read task exits via `OperationCanceledException` rather than a socket exception. `ForceDisconnect` is still called from the `finally` block of the read loop to cover the remote-close case.

## Test plan

- [ ] Build passes with 0 errors
- [ ] Auth flow: client connects, `ClientHelloAuth` dispatched correctly
- [ ] World flow: character select and world entry work end-to-end
- [ ] Fragmented packet: large packet split across multiple TCP segments reassembles correctly
- [ ] Clean disconnect: client close and server-initiated disconnect both exit the read loop without error logs

Closes #477

This PR implements the "who" commands, which were added in #529 

There are 3 WIP tags in this PR that I would like other members of the community to look at before this can be merged. 

The first tag deals with the data structure I am iterating over for the who command themselves. The PlayerManager looked like a proper thread safe alternative to my earlier IWorldSessions implementation, but it seemed as though @Rawaho was indicating I should make a separate manager for players that only updates when a relevant who query changes. 

The next tag deals with my inability to pass subzone queries via the search parameters. I have failed to do this with both the explicit query parameter "Zone" and the implicit "Combo" query parameter that attempts to parse zone data from a string. I need some guidance to get this working as I have not been able to trigger any sub zone queries so far.

The final tag deals with whether or not we should restrict string length for search queries similar to how WoW limits the string length to queries that are strictly greater than 2 characters. The client allows users to pass lower length strings so my instinct is to support all lengths of strings that the client will accept and pass to the server.

recent.title: [feat] Add Docker Compose stack for full server deployment
recent.head: 114f6eacb6013f625f7a0647da6a3468586ca1f0
recent.body:
**Add Docker Compose stack for full server deployment**

Introduces a complete Docker-based setup that mirrors the [official NexusForever server guide](https://www.emulator.ws/installation/server-guide), allowing the entire server stack to be stood up with a single command.

## What's included

**docker-compose.yml** — Orchestrates all services with explicit dependency ordering:
- **Infrastructure:** MariaDB 11.4 (fixed IP `172.26.240.10`) and RabbitMQ 3.13
- **One-shot setup:** `init` → `migrate` → `world-import` → `check-assets` pipeline that runs automatically before game servers start
- **Game servers:** `auth`, `sts`, `character-api`, `group` (default); `world`, `chat` (`--profile game`)
- **Tools:** `extractor`, `build-artifacts`, `launcher` (`--profile tools`)
- `auth` uses `socat` to relay `127.0.0.1:24000 → world:24000` for client compatibility

**init.sh**
- Generates all `docker/config/*.json` from `Source/**/*.example.json` via `jq` (substitutes DB, RabbitMQ, Character API connection details)
- Clones `NexusForever.WorldDatabase` and checks out a pinned revision (`342cb2e`) — the last commit fully covered by EF migrations

**import.sh**
- Imports all world database SQL files into `nexus_forever_world` after migrations complete
- Runs as a separate `world-import` service to enforce correct sequencing
- Captures and prints MariaDB error output per-file with a final error count summary

**migrate.sh**
- Installs `dotnet-ef` and runs `database update` for all five `DbContext`s (`Auth`, `Character`, `World`, `Chat`, `Group`)
- Runs from `/migrate-config` (mounted config) so design-time factories resolve JSON config files without touching the source tree

**01-databases.sql**
- Bootstrapped by MariaDB on first volume creation — creates all five databases and the `nexusforever` user

**README.md**
- Full reference for every file in docker, including all generated/gitignored paths (`config/`, `game-data/`, `world-database/`) with creation instructions and per-service usage

## Usage

```bash
# First time setup + game servers
docker compose up -d                        # runs init → migrate → world-import → check-assets
docker compose --profile game up -d        # starts world + chat after assets pass

# Extract game assets from WildStar client
WILDSTAR_DIR=/path/to/WildStar docker compose --profile tools run --rm extractor
```

Port bindings, credentials, and `WILDSTAR_DIR` are all overridable via .env.

recent.title: Add loot system enum types to Game.Static
recent.head: 8861e08ea1356df952629a39d3e648d31fb2677e
recent.body:
## Summary

Adds three new enums to `NexusForever.Game.Static/Loot/` that are prerequisites for loot system implementation:

- **`LootEntityType`** — Distinguishes creature vs item loot sources. Used by the loot manager to route drops through the correct lookup table (entity_loot vs item_loot).
- **`LooterType`** — Player/Group/Raid/Guild distribution modes. Determines loot visibility and distribution rules per loot instance.
- **`LootConditionType`** — 9 condition types for conditional loot group evaluation (class, race, level range, quest completion/objective state). Used by loot groups to filter drops based on player state.

### Why these values

All values are derived from client data tables (specifically the loot group condition system visible in quest reward filtering and creature loot tables). `LootItemType` and `LootRollAction` already exist in Game.Static with identical values — verified, no changes needed.

### What this enables

These types are the static foundation for a full loot system: loot tables, drop generation, conditional filtering, and group loot distribution. No runtime code depends on these yet — this is purely additive.

recent.title: Apply Armor Pierce before mitigation by reducing effective armor
recent.head: 4bda9d1269fda8464c8cf7686ff3743b6edeae91
recent.body:
This integrates Armor Pierce into the damage mitigation calculation.

Current behavior:
- Armor mitigation is calculated using victim armor only
- RatingArmorPierce exists in the stat system but is not used in mitigation

Change:
- Reads attacker Armor Pierce via GetRatingPercentMod(Property.RatingArmorPierce, attacker)
- Reduces victim effective armor before mitigation calculation:
  effectiveArmor = armor × (1 - armorPiercePct)

Notes:
- This follows the character sheet representation of Armor Pierce as a percentage
- This does not yet include Strikethrough overflow contributing to Armor Pierce
- Implementation assumes Armor Pierce reduces effective armor rather than mitigation directly

Happy to adjust if a different design was intended.
